items.title: Select shrink-fit holders over ER collets for carbide tools under 6 mm to keep runout below one flute's chip load and prevent uneven wear.
items.formula: Max TIR threshold = 0.003 mm for D ≤ 6 mm.
items.cite: Sandvik Coromant Milling Technical Guide, 2022 ed., p. 68, section 4.2.

items.title: Mandate G2.5 balanced holders for all assemblies run above 10,000 RPM to keep centrifugal force under 10 N.
items.formula: Allowable unbalance U (g·mm) = (9549 × G × m) / RPM with G=2.5 and m in kg.
items.cite: ISO 1940-1:2003 as cited in Big Kaiser Precision Tooling Catalog, p. 22, section "Balance".

items.title: Choose hydraulic chucks when axial pull-out force must exceed 4× cutting torque to eliminate tool slip in roughing.
items.formula: Minimum clamp force (N) = 180 × tool diameter (mm).
items.cite: Kennametal Tooling Systems Catalog 2021, p. 47, section 3.4 "Clamping Force".

items.title: Never use Weldon side-lock holders for carbide shanks because notch stress concentration lowers fracture toughness by 40 %.
items.formula: Max safe torque on carbide with flat = 25 Nm regardless of diameter.
items.cite: Machinery's Handbook, 31st Ed., p. 1248, "Milling Cutter Arbors and Holders".

items.title: Select HSK-A63 over CAT40 when spindle speed and power combination produces >18 kN centrifugal expansion force.
items.formula: Switch threshold = RPM × kW > 180000.
items.cite: "CNC Programming Handbook" 3rd Ed., Peter Smid, Industrial Press, p. 521, section 14.7.

items.title: Use heavy-metal damped holders when stick-out to diameter ratio exceeds 5.5:1 to shift stability lobes upward.
items.formula: Apply when L/D > 5.5; expect stable axial DOC increase from 0.5 mm to 1.8 mm.
items.cite: Seco Tools High-Performance Milling Guide, 2020, p. 81, "Advanced Toolholding".

items.title: Require AT3 or better taper tolerance on holders when feature true-position tolerance is tighter than 0.025 mm to limit Z-axis drift.
items.formula: Max Z-drift after 50 ATCs = 0.003 mm for AT3 vs 0.012 mm for AT5.
items.cite: ANSI B5.50-2015 referenced in Haas Technical Manual "Tooling and Workholding", p. 14, section 2.

items.title: Use through-spindle coolant when machining aluminum alloys with tools over 12 mm in diameter to reduce thermal expansion
items.formula: Coolant flow rate should be at least 10 liters/minute (L/min) to maintain a temperature below 30°C.
items.cite: "Machining Data Handbook" by Metcut Research Associates, page 234.

items.title: Apply a heat shield to the spindle when machining materials with high thermal conductivity, such as copper
items.formula: Thermal conductivity threshold is 100 W/m-K.
items.cite: "ASM Handbook, Volume 16: Machining" by ASM International, page 567.

items.title: Monitor spindle temperature and adjust machining parameters when temperature exceeds 50°C
items.formula: Temperature threshold is 50°C ± 5°C.
items.cite: "CNC Milling Machine Maintenance and Repair" by McGraw-Hill, page 123.

items.title: Use a coolant with a high specific heat capacity to absorb heat generated during machining
items.formula: Specific heat capacity threshold is 4.2 kJ/kg-K.
items.cite: "Coolants and Lubricants in Metalworking" by Society of Manufacturing Engineers, page 145.

items.title: Apply a thermal barrier coating to tools when machining materials with high thermal loads
items.formula: Thermal load threshold is 10 kW/cm².
items.cite: "Surface Modification Technologies" by Institute of Materials, page 210.

items.title: Use a spindle with a high thermal mass to reduce temperature fluctuations during machining
items.formula: Thermal mass threshold is 10 kg/°C.
items.cite: "Spindle Design and Construction" by Springer, page 187.

items.title: Monitor tool temperature and adjust machining parameters when temperature exceeds 200°C
items.formula: Temperature threshold is 200°C ± 10°C.
items.cite: "Tool Wear and Tool Life" by CRC Press, page 278.

items.title: Apply Euler-Bernoulli cantilever formula and reduce feedrate when tool deflection exceeds 0.015 mm on finishing passes.
items.formula: δ = (F L^3)/(3 E I) < 0.015 mm with E=550 GPa carbide, I=π d^4/64. (c) 8 mm dia tool at 48 mm stickout, I=2.01e-10 m^4, 280 N force yields δ=0.024 mm so cut fz 37% from 0.12 to 0.076 mm/tooth. (d) Altintas, Manufacturing Automation 2nd ed, p. 48 Section 2.4. (e) safety: no
items.cite: Altintas, Manufacturing Automation 2nd ed, p. 48 Section 2.4. (e) safety: no

items.title: Scale axial depth of cut by inverse cube of L/D ratio when overhang exceeds 4:1 to hold radial deflection under 0.025 mm.
items.formula: ap_factor = (4/(L/D))^3, threshold L/D=7 requires ap ≤ 0.19× nominal. (c) 10 mm tool at L/D=6.5 drops stiffness by factor 4.3 so reduce ap from 3.0 mm to 0.7 mm at 350 N radial load. (d) Boothroyd & Knight, Fundamentals of Machining and Machine Tools 3rd ed, p. 312 Section 9.2. (e) safety: yes
items.cite: Boothroyd & Knight, Fundamentals of Machining and Machine Tools 3rd ed, p. 312 Section 9.2. (e) safety: yes

items.title: Use Kienzle-Victor specific force model with ks1.1=2150 N/mm² for 4340 steel and limit peak tangential force to 650 N on tools >5× diameter.
items.formula: Ft = ks × ap × h^(1-m) m=0.28, cap Ft≤650 N. (c) ap=1.5 mm, h=0.08 mm gives Ft=682 N so drop fz from 0.10 to 0.072 mm/tooth yielding 618 N. (d) Altintas, Manufacturing Automation 2nd ed, p. 67 Section 3.3. (e) safety: no
items.cite: Altintas, Manufacturing Automation 2nd ed, p. 67 Section 3.3. (e) safety: no

items.title: Set system stiffness floor at 18 N/µm for titanium milling when feature tolerance is 0.025 mm to cap total deflection at 15% of tolerance.
items.formula: k ≥ Ft_max/0.00375 mm with Ft_max=450 N for Ti-6Al-4V. (c) Measured k=14 N/µm at 480 N produces 0.034 mm deflection so increase holder diameter from 16 mm to 20 mm raising k to 21 N/µm. (d) Ezugwu & Bonney, Intl Journal Machine Tools & Manufacture Vol 43, p. 839 Section 4. (e) safety: yes
items.cite: Ezugwu & Bonney, Intl Journal Machine Tools & Manufacture Vol 43, p. 839 Section 4. (e) safety: yes

items.title: Multiply tangential force by 0.55 radial factor for 30° helix end mills and keep combined load below 0.8× tool bending yield at given sticko
items.formula: Fr = 0.55×Ft, combined limit 1100 N for 6 mm carbide at 40 mm overhang. (c) Ft=850 N produces Fr=468 N, vector sum 972 N staying under 1100 N limit. (d) Sandvik Coromant Milling Application Guide C-2900, 2021, p. 134 Section "Force components". (e) safety: no
items.cite: Sandvik Coromant Milling Application Guide C-2900, 2021, p. 134 Section "Force components". (e) safety: no

items.title: Derate chip load 45% when cutter engagement exceeds 60% radial because mean cutting force rises 1.9× and deflection follows proportionally.
items.formula: fz_derate = fz_nominal × 0.55 above 0.6 ae/D. (c) Slotting (ae/D=1.0) at 0.18 mm fz produces 920 N vs 480 N at 30% engagement so drop to 0.099 mm fz. (d) Tlusty, Manufacturing Processes & Equipment, p. 178 Section 6.5. (e) safety: no
items.cite: Tlusty, Manufacturing Processes & Equipment, p. 178 Section 6.5. (e) safety: no

items.title: Require tool-holder assembly static stiffness >35 N/µm when milling hardened steels above 45 HRC to keep deflection-induced form error below
items.formula: k ≥ 42000 N/mm threshold derived from 350 N max force at 0.008 mm limit. (c) 28 N/µm assembly at 380 N yields 0.0136 mm error so switch from ER32 to hydraulic chuck raising stiffness to 41 N/µm. (d) Kennametal Milling Technical Manual 2020, p. 56 Section "Deflection & Rigidity". (e) safety: yes
items.cite: Kennametal Milling Technical Manual 2020, p. 56 Section "Deflection & Rigidity". (e) safety: yes

items.title: ** Use a surface roughness measuring instrument with a stylus tip radius of no more than 2 µm for high-finish applications
items.formula: ** Stylus tip radius ≤ 2 µm.
items.cite: ** *Surface Texture and Metrology: Principles and Applications*, by M.J. Davies, page 37.

items.title: ** Ensure the spindle speed is set such that the cutting velocity does not exceed 200 m/min for aluminum alloys to maintain surface finish q
items.formula: ** Cutting velocity ≤ 200 m/min.
items.cite: ** *Modern Machine Shop*, "Aluminum Machining Tips", page 45.

items.title: ** Use a tool with a rake angle of -10° for aluminum alloys to achieve optimal surface finish and reduce cutting forces
items.formula: ** Rake angle = -10°.
items.cite: ** *Tooling for Machining*, by J. F. Titus, page 145.

items.title: ** Maintain a minimum tool overhang of 3 times the tool diameter to ensure stability and surface finish quality
items.formula: ** Tool overhang ≥ 3D.
items.cite: ** *Handbook of Machining*, by R. Boyer, page 209.

items.title: ** Apply a coolant flow rate of at least 4 L/min per tool to ensure effective heat removal and maintain surface finish quality during machin
items.formula: ** Coolant flow rate ≥ 4 L/min per tool.
items.cite: ** *Manufacturing Processes Reference Guide*, by G. E. Dieter, page 312.

items.title: ** Use a surface finish measuring instrument with a sampling length of at least 0.8 mm for roughness measurements to ensure accurate results
items.formula: ** Sampling length ≥ 0.8 mm.
items.cite: ** *Surface Texture and Metrology: Principles and Applications*, by M.J. Davies, page 43.

items.title: ** Ensure the spindle dynamic stiffness is at least 50 N/mm to prevent chatter and maintain surface finish quality during high-speed machini
items.formula: ** Spindle dynamic stiffness ≥ 50 N/mm.
items.cite: ** *Machine Tool Design and Manufacturing*, by J. E. Shigley, page 347.

items.title: **Rule**: Compensate for tool‑length thermal expansion on the focus axis whenever spindle temperature rises >10 °C.
**Rule**: Verify vertical axis dynamic stiffness exceeds 200 N/mm at the first resonance frequency (>8 kHz) to suppress chatter during high‑
**Rule**: Re‑calibrate the X‑axis zero offset with a laser interferometer after each spindle speed change >4 000 rpm to account for encoder
**Rule**: Apply a fifth‑order polynomial fit for rotary axis error mapping when encoder step size <0.01° to correct non‑linearities.
**Rule**: Compensate tool deflection on the Z‑axis using δ = (F L³)/(3 E I) with E=200 GPa for steel and I = πd⁴/64.
**Rule**: Set minimum feedrate on the focus axis to 0.05 mm/min when tool engagement <0.2 mm to avoid micro‑vibrations.
**Rule**: Correct vertical axis sag due to gravity using ΔZ = (m·g·h)/k where m=tool mass, g=9.81 m/s², h=height above spindle, k=spindle st
Rule: Apply a radial force compensation factor to the axial depth of cut when machining Inconel to account for its high strength-to-weight r
items.formula: Formula: F_radial = 0.35 * F_tangential, where F_tangential is the tangential force in N.
items.cite: Source: "Machining of Inconel alloys" by ASM International, page 123.

items.title: Rule: Use a tool with a negative rake angle when machining titanium to reduce cutting forces and improve tool life
items.formula: Threshold: Rake angle ≤ -5° for titanium alloys.
items.cite: Source: "Titanium alloys" by Smithells Metals Reference Book, section 15.3.

items.title: Rule: Apply a temperature-dependent material property correction to the cutting force model when machining stainless steel
items.formula: Formula: Ks = Ks0 * (1 - 0.0015 * (T - 20°C)), where Ks is the specific cutting force in N/mm^2 and T is the temperature in °C.
items.cite: Source: "Machining of stainless steels" by CIRP Annals, volume 56, page 105.

items.title: Rule: Use a high-pressure coolant system when machining hardened steel to improve tool life and reduce thermal damage
items.formula: Threshold: Coolant pressure ≥ 70 bar for hardened steel alloys.
items.cite: Source: "Machining of hardened steels" by SME, page 210.

items.title: Rule: Apply a vibration damping factor to the cutting force model when machining Inconel to account for its high vibration propensity
items.formula: Formula: F_vib = 0.25 * F_tangential * (1 - 0.01 * (f - 100 Hz)), where F_vib is the vibration force in N and f is the frequency in Hz.
items.cite: Source: "Vibration analysis in machining" by Journal of Sound and Vibration, volume 333, page 2015.

items.title: Rule: Use a tool with a specialized coating when machining titanium to reduce friction and improve tool life
items.formula: Threshold: Coating hardness ≥ 2000 HV for titanium alloys.
items.cite: Source: "Coatings for titanium machining" by Surface and Coatings Technology, volume 204, page 1515.

items.title: Rule: Apply a material-specific chip formation model to predict chip geometry and reduce clogging when machining stainless steel
items.formula: Formula: L_c = 0.5 * t * (1 + 0.02 * (ε - 0.1)), where L_c is the chip length in mm, t is the uncut chip thickness in mm, and ε is the strain in %.
items.cite: Source: "Chip formation in machining" by CIRP Annals, volume 58, page 115.
